dossier.public_summary: This is an on-target 12-minute dip that looks flat-bottomed but is seen to be more than ten times deeper and then almost invisible in different TESS sectors, including within the same pipeline. The change is real, not a calibration offset, and the star shows strong out-of-transit brightness swings. A stable planet must keep the same depth; what is seen instead is variable systematics or variability.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 418.6% across sectors (123 ppm in sector 10, 176 ppm in sector 37, 1185 ppm in sector 64, 60 ppm in sector 99, 38 ppm in sector 100, 62 ppm in sector 101).
Depth changes within the same light-curve product, ruling out calibration. TESS-SPOC alone varies from 176 ppm (err 47) to 1185 ppm (err 62); QLP steady at 53 ppm (err 24).
Large out-of-dip swing, ratio_to_depth 0.6687 with chi2 60.77 for 7 dof, indicating variability/binary rather than transits.

Difference imaging on the target with offset 10.61 arcsec err 6.112 sigma 1.736 puts the dip on the star and excludes neighbours that could cause it (plausible_within_1px 0). The depth change is therefore on-target variability, consistent with a systematics or blended-eclipse varying with aperture/sector, not a stable planet.
Low planet-like score consistent with variable-depth false positives.
